answer: On each agent's first voyage through the network, identity is not free: they must deposit a shale-layer of bonded stake that only unlocks after sustained peer attestation. New accounts sit in a shallow oasis of limited influence until their bond ages and countersignatures accumulate, so spinning up thousands of shells costs real capital and time rather than free compute. Sybils starve because the bond pool and attestation lag scale faster than clone creation.
